newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Commerzbank plans standby loan for Czech Agrobanka.
newsitem.headline: Commerzbank plans standby loan for Czech Agrobanka.

text.p: Germany's Commerzbank AG said on Tuesday it has offered a two billion crown credit to be guaranteed by the Czech National Bank (CNB) to Agrobanka a.s. which is under CNB administration with liquidity problems.

Commerzbank spokesman Ulrich Ramm told Reuters that the CNB had reacted favourably to the plan -- for what he said could be considered a stand-by credit for Agrobanka -- and that it was "accepted in principle".
"It is, up to now, an idea extended to the central bank, and the central bank is very pleased," Ramm said after a news conference to open Commerzbank's new Prague office.
No central bank official was immediately available for comment.

Ramm said that so far none of the money had been disbursed. Commerzbank saw the offer as a "possible expression of Commerzbank's involvement in the Czech Republic" and helping the stability of the banking sector.
Agrobanka was put under temporary forced administration by the Czech National Bank in September after running into liquidity problems.
It is the country's fifth largest bank and the largest fully-private Czech bank.
Ramm said the interest rate on the loan would be "in line with money market rates for a top borrower because it has a central bank guarantee."
Asked at the news conference whether Commerzbank might want a stake in Agrobanka, Commerzbank chairman Martin Kohlhaussen said: "A clear answer is no. There is no interest to invest in Agrobanka.
"We have decided, quite voluntarily, and without being requested to do so, to provide support for Agrobanka," said Kohlhaussen.

He said many people were now doubting the rectitude of the market reforms of Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus's centre-right government but he urged Czech officials to keep a cool head and push on with reform.
"We do not share such doubts. There is no reasonable alternative to the path taken by the Czech Republic up to now," he said.

"If it (the Czech Republic) stays the course without wavering -- and that is what official sources repeatedly claim -- these teething troubles of a market economy system will be overcome," Kohlhaussen added.
Commerzbank had guaranteed two 100 million mark bond issues for the former Czechoslovakia, the obligations on which were assumed by the Czech Republic after the split with Slovakia in 1993.
